title: From cost to the right price, and what discounts really cost

say: From cost to the right price, and what discounts really cost.
This is the video for Module 2 of Introduction to Pricing and Selling.
In Module 1 you found your true cost. Now you turn it into a price.
Cost-plus pricing starts from your cost and adds a chosen percentage. It tells you the lowest price you can accept.

say: Say a pack costs you 550 naira and you sell it for 800 naira. Your profit is 250 naira.
Markup compares that profit with your cost. 250 divided by 550 is a markup of about 45%.

panel.heading: Markup versus margin
right: Share of each sale you keep

say: Margin compares the same profit with your price. 250 divided by 800 is a margin of about 31%.
Both are correct. Trouble starts when you mix them up.

panel.heading: Markup versus margin
right: Share of each sale you keep

say: Here is the method. Start with your true cost per item from Module 1.

panel.heading: Pricing for a target margin
items: Start with your true cost per item
Price = cost divided by (1 minus margin)
Round to an easy price to pay
Recheck profit and margin after rounding

say: To keep a target margin, divide your cost by 1 minus that margin. For a 30% margin on 550 naira, divide 550 by 0.70. That gives about 785 naira.

panel.heading: Pricing for a target margin
items: Start with your true cost per item
Price = cost divided by (1 minus margin)
Round to an easy price to pay
Recheck profit and margin after rounding

say: Round to a figure that is easy to pay and give change for, such as 800 naira.

panel.heading: Pricing for a target margin
items: Start with your true cost per item
Price = cost divided by (1 minus margin)
Round to an easy price to pay
Recheck profit and margin after rounding

say: Then recheck. Rounding up is usually safe, but rounding down can eat your margin.

panel.heading: Pricing for a target margin
items: Start with your true cost per item

say: Now the trap. If you simply add 30% to 550 naira, you get 715 naira. Your real margin is only 23%, not 30%.

Recheck profit and margin after rounding
panel.rule: Adding 30% to cost does not give you a 30% margin.

say: Next, survey the market. List the sellers your customers could buy from instead of you, and compare like with like.

say: Ngozi divides each price by the size. Seller A works out at 400 naira per 100 g, Seller B at 360 naira, and Seller C, with a branded tub, at 600 naira.

say: So do personal service and trust. For example, Amaka the tailor delivers in 3 days with a proper fitting, so she charges 18,000 naira for a gown that costs her 11,000 naira.
Charge only for real benefits. Never exaggerate.

say: A discount comes straight out of your profit, not out of your cost.
If Ngozi gives 10% off, her price falls by 80 naira to 720 naira. Her cost stays the same, so her profit falls from 250 naira to 170 naira. She has lost 32% of her profit on that pack.
Here is the extra sales rule. Divide the old profit by the new profit. 250 divided by 170 is 1.47.
So if she normally sells 100 packs a week, she must sell about 147 packs just to stand still.
Give a discount only when it is paid for by a real saving, like one delivery for a bulk order. A free item costs you its cost, not its price, so buy 10 get 1 free can beat 10% off.
Set time limits, write your walk-away price, and never go below your floor.

panel.heading: Protect your margin
items: Discount only for real savings or volume
Buy 10, get 1 free can beat 10% off
Set a time limit on offers
Write your walk-away price
Never go below your price floor

say: To remember. Price for a margin by dividing cost by 1 minus the margin. Markup and margin are not the same.
Cost sets the floor, competitors show the range, and value places you in it. Discounts come out of profit, so check the extra sales you would need first.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Margin price = cost divided by (1 minus margin)
Markup is profit over cost; margin is profit over price
Cost sets the floor, competitors the range, value your place
A discount comes out of profit, not cost
Extra sales needed = old profit divided by new profit
